n=512/1024 trailing Householder update GEMM currently runs fp16x3 (3 MMAs). On CUDA-13 B200 FP8 e4m3 tensor cores are 2x FP16 / 4x TF32 (3851 TFLOPS). Swap the dominant trailing update to a single block-scaled FP8 e4m3 MMA (per-tile amax scaling to use the e4m3 range), and add a cheap on-device per-matrix factor-residual check that re-runs ONLY the matrices that miss the 20*n*eps tolerance at fp16x3. The loose tol + 1/n error shrink should let most well-conditioned matrices pass at FP8, cutting trailing cost ~2x where it dominates.

Scaffolding: FP8 e4m3 trailing dot helpers (fp8x2/x3/x4, per-tile amax-scaled hi+lo splits) wired as IPREC/DPREC modes into _trailing_fused_kernel. Defaults unchanged -> benchmark byte-identical at 2187us. Key finding: uniform fp8x3 on n=512 trailing is SLOWER (5210 vs 3964us fp16x3) -- the trailing is overhead/latency-bound not tensor-bound, so per-tile amax+cast overhead dominates and e4m3's 2x throughput never materializes at BLK=32 tiles. Only fewer-MMA fp8 (x1/x2) could win.

FP8 e4m3 trailing: measured NEGATIVE result, kept off by default. Removed fp8fx diagnostic; kept fp8/x2/x3/x4 reachable via QR_*_F_PREC (off default). VERDICT (isolated contention-free n512 dense B640): fp16(1MMA)=3877us PASS, fp16x3(3MMA)=4157us, fp8(1MMA, the brief's exact proposal)=4325us FAIL, fp8x2=4809us, fp8x3=5219us PASS. A single e4m3 MMA is SLOWER than a single fp16 MMA (and fixed-scale e4m3 w/o amax slower still) -> the n512/1024 trailing is latency/pipeline/register-bound not tensor-bound, so e4m3's 2x FLOPS never materialize while its cast+amax+regs are pure cost. Every FP8 mode dominated by fp16 analog at equal MMA count -> no per-matrix re-run can win (even all-pass single-MMA FP8 costs more than the fp16 floor). validate PASS all guards; benchmark 2193us == baseline (perf-neutral).

Brief-0 FP8 e4m3 trailing: NEGATIVE result, no improvement (best=baseline 2193us, perf-neutral). The brief's premise is FALSIFIED by measurement: isolated n512 dense B640 -- fp16(1MMA)=3877us, fp16x3(3MMA)=4157us, fp8(1MMA, the exact 'single block-scaled e4m3 MMA + per-tile amax' proposed)=4325us(FAIL acc), fp8x2=4809us, fp8x3=5219us(PASS acc). A single e4m3 MMA is SLOWER than a single fp16 MMA, and fixed-scale e4m3 (no amax) is slower still, so the n512/1024 trailing is latency/pipeline/register-bound NOT tensor-bound (matches env's ~36% SM throughput note) -- e4m3's 2x FLOPS are irrelevant here while its cast+amax+register-pressure are pure cost. Every FP8 mode is dominated by the fp16 analog at equal MMA count, so the per-matrix residual re-run cannot win: even the all-pass best case (single-MMA FP8) costs more than the fp16 floor. The accuracy ladder DID work as hypothesized (FP8x3 passes well-conditioned dense at scaled_factor ~9 vs gate 20, fails ill-conditioned) -- the kill is purely the wall-time, not correctness. Committed FP8 helpers (_dot_fp8/x2/x3/x4) as off-by-default selectable IPREC modes documenting the dead end. validate PASS all guards. SUGGESTIONS for next briefs: (1) the n512 trailing is NOT tensor-bound, so precision swaps are a dead end there -- attack the latency/pipeline/register binding instead (occupancy, scheduling, fewer launches). (2) NOTABLE: fp16(1MMA)=3877us beats the current fp16x3(3MMA)=4157us default on dense by ~7% -- a single fp16 MMA is faster; if a per-matrix residual re-run gated single-fp16-MMA sweep1 (recompute only ill-conditioned matrices at fp16x3) were free enough, it could net a real win on the dense-dominated shapes (3,4,9,10,11). The re-run machinery I scoped (device-side eff-rank-style redo[B] + fp16x3 fixup grid with per-block early-out, graph-capture-safe like the existing RANKSKIP) would apply directly -- just with fp16x1 not fp8 as the fast path. (3) leaderboard #1 (10billiontokens s28.py)=1293us vs our #6 1723us; #7 is levidiamode mxfp10.py=1944us (FP-microscaling, but NOT leading) -- confirms FP8/MX is legal but not the frontier approach; the gap to #1 is structural, not a precision tweak.

Your own brief-0 side-finding is a LIVE win: plain fp16 (1 MMA) trailing = 3877us beats the fp16x3 (3 MMA) default = 4157us by ~7% on dense, because the trailing is latency-bound so FEWER MMAs win. Land it: make trailing sweep-1 run fp16x1 (single MMA) as the FAST path, add the device-side per-matrix factor-residual classifier + redo[B] fixup grid you already scoped, and re-run ONLY the ill-conditioned matrices (rankdef/clustered/mixc) at fp16x3. Default-ON. Target the dense-dominated shapes 3,4,7,9,10,11 for a real geomean drop; keep all guards PASS.

fp16x1/x2 trailing win is ILLUSORY under correctness; classifier UNBUILDABLE. Measured sweep-1-only n512 dense: fp16x3=3967/fp16x2=3917/fp16=3863us. BUT: fp16x1 FAILS band+rowscale TEST shapes (B=16) outright; fp16x2 FAILS diff_guard (1 matrix scaled=20.6 vs gate 20 on a mixed rotation, B=640) -- re-confirms brief-65 tf32x2 rejection. Brief-1 fp16x1 trailing win: NO improvement landed (best=baseline 2177us). The brief-0 side-finding does NOT survive correctness enforcement, and I proved this rigorously with ground-truth validate. SWEEP-1-ONLY n512 dense wall: fp16x3=3967 / fp16x2=3917(-1.3%) / fp16=3863(-2.6%)us -- but: (a) fp16x1 FAILS the n512 band(seed32527)+rowscale(seed32528) TEST shapes at B=16 OUTRIGHT (hard validate fail, not marginal); (b) fp16x2 FAILS the diff_correctness_guard -- a  rotation of the clustered bench shape lands ONE matrix at scaled=20.6 (gate 20, B=640). My brief-0 3877-vs-4157 'win' was inflated: it changed BOTH sweeps (sweep-2 is already fp16x1 by default, so the only lever is sweep-1) and had contention; the clean sweep-1-only delta is small AND unsafe. This INDEPENDENTLY RE-CONFIRMS the prior fleet's brief-65 rejection of 2-MMA sweep-1 (tf32x2 failed the diff-guard at 20.6 on a timed mixed matrix -- I hit the EXACT same failure mode with fp16x2). THE PER-MATRIX REDO IS UNBUILDABLE: no cheap false-negative-free classifier separates the marginal (~3% over gate, single-matrix) failures. I tested four: (1) exact ||R-Q^T A||_1 via householder_product = 216ms (cuSOLVER serially loops the batch -- the launch wall the kernel exists to avoid); (2) kappa=max|Rii|/min|Rii| is UNSOUND -- well-conditioned dense reaches kappa 1e5-1e7 and PASSES while failing band sits at kappa 1.6e3, so catching band flags ALL of dense -> full redo -> slower than fp16x3 (conditioning != fp16x1-error: rankdef passes at kappa 1e31); (3) 16-probe random residual OVERLAPS on band (the L1 gate is worst-case row-sum, the probe estimates spectral/Frobenius avg); (4) per-panel error-feedback sum ||fp16x1_delta - fp32_delta||_1 OVERLAPS (final residual depends on AMPLIFICATION through later panels, not injected magnitude -- band passing 117 > band failing 102). Committed comment-only doc (default stays fp16x3, code byte-identical to validated parent 306660c4); recorded all four dead classifiers inline so no future brief re-explores. n1024 ALSO has no win: tf32rn(1MMA)=3911 already BEATS fp16/x2/x3 (3973/4016/4137) -- device-underfill-bound, not precision-bound. SUGGESTIONS: (1) fp16x3 is the IRREDUCIBLE precision floor for the n512 sweep-1; STOP probing trailing precision -- it's a closed dead end (brief-0 fp8 + brief-1 fp16x1/x2 both confirm latency-bound, not tensor/precision-bound). (2) The real lever on n512 (grid-saturated, latency-bound) is OCCUPANCY/SCHEDULING/LAUNCH-COUNT, and on n1024/n2048 (underfill-bound) is FILLING IDLE SMs (env notes ~88 idle SMs at n1024; the never-landed multi-CTA-per-matrix m-split with ~59% headroom is the standing big idea). (3) Gap to #1 (10billiontokens s28.py=1293us vs our #6 1723us) is structural; precision micro-tuning of an already-near-optimal trailing cannot close it.

n=512 panel is register-walled (21% occ, 0.62 issued-warps/sched, short_scoreboard-dominated = smem-reduction latency); grid is SATURATED so the cure is cross-matrix ILP, not more CTAs. W4's Triton 2-matrix packing FAILED only because tl.sum is BLOCK-cooperative (packed matrices sync at the reduction). Fix it in HAND-WRITTEN CUDA: one CTA owns 2-4 matrices, each matrix assigned to its OWN warp-group doing WARP-PRIVATE shuffle reductions (no block barrier), so warp-group j's trailing-apply hides warp-group i's reflector-reduction latency. Keep the packed panel UN-SPILLED (W4's dual-tile-pack spilled -> stage in smem or narrow per-matrix register tiles). Outputs byte-compatible with the Triton trailing. Target n=512 B=640; exact geqrf (H,tau); all guards PASS.

Cross-matrix-ILP CUDA panel: BUILT + bit-compatible (3 variants, H/tau/V/T ~4e-6 vs Triton) but measured NET LOSS. The ILP mechanism WORKS (MWG=2 ~20% faster than MWG=1; named-barrier per-warp-group sync fixes W4's tl.sum blocker), but all hand variants are 5-7x SLOWER than the Triton panel (Triton 64us vs CUDA smem=320/reg-resident=431/1warp=391us, pheight=512 B=640). Root kill: the unblocked panel does ~500 full-height reductions/sub-panel, and hand cross-warp reduction (shfl+smem+named-barrier) is 5-7x slower per reduction than Triton tl.sum codegen; 20% ILP can't overcome that. Register-residency didn't help (bottleneck is reduction throughput not data movement; 256-reg tile craters occ). Default unchanged (comment-only, code byte-identical to baseline), benchmark 2180us. To beat Triton panel needs an algorithmic cut in #reductions, not latency-hiding.

Brief-2 cross-matrix-ILP CUDA panel: NO improvement landed (baseline 2180us). I fully BUILT the brief's idea -- a hand-written CUDA panel-factor kernel packing several matrices per CTA, each warp-group doing warp-private reductions via NAMED BARRIERS (bar.sync id,nthreads per group, no block-wide sync) -- in THREE variants (smem-staged, register-resident, one-warp-per-matrix), all proven BIT-COMPATIBLE with the Triton _panel_factor2_kernel (H/tau/V/T match ~4e-6, inside 20*n*eps). Two confirmations for the brief: (1) the cross-matrix-ILP MECHANISM WORKS -- MWG=2 (2 matrices/CTA) measured ~20% faster than MWG=1 on the j=0 pheight=512 sub-panel, the latency-hiding the brief predicted; (2) the named-barrier per-warp-group sync GENUINELY FIXES W4's tl.sum-is-block-cooperative blocker (each group syncs independently). BUT IT IS A NET LOSS: every hand variant is 5-7x SLOWER than the Triton panel (Triton 64us vs CUDA smem-staged 320us / register-resident 431us / one-warp 391us, all on the SAME pheight=512 B=640 sub-panel). ROOT KILL (the real finding): the unblocked panel needs a FULL-HEIGHT reduction at EVERY reflector build AND every column apply AND every T-dot -- ~500 reductions per sub-panel -- and a hand-written cross-warp reduction (warp-shuffle + smem rbuf + named-barrier round-trip) is 5-7x slower PER REDUCTION than Triton's tl.sum codegen. A 20% cross-matrix-ILP win cannot overcome a 5-7x per-reduction throughput deficit. Critically, REGISTER-RESIDENCY (holding the panel in registers exactly like Triton, NOT in smem) did NOT close the gap -- proving the bottleneck is reduction THROUGHPUT, not panel data movement, and the 256-reg/thread tile craters occupancy. The panel is 33.4% of n512 (1354us, torch-profiler) so the prize was real, but the Triton register-tensor panel is simply the better realization here. Committed comment-only (code byte-identical to baseline dc53a9f12); the working CUDA kernels + the two correctness lessons (no divergent shfl/bar.sync; __syncwarp between strided-store and cross-lane-read) are documented inline for any future attempt. SUGGESTIONS: (1) The panel's wall is the NUMBER of full-height reductions (~500/sub-panel), not their latency -- so the win is ALGORITHMIC: a panel formulation with FEWER syncs/reductions (e.g. a fully-register-blocked-within-panel scheme that batches multiple reflector reductions, or a recursive/communication-avoiding panel), NOT cross-matrix ILP on the same reduction count. (2) Alternatively attack n512's OTHER 67%: the trailing is precision-floored (brief-0/1 closed) but the DtoD memcpy is 215us/5.3% (the clone-fusion may have a residual copy) and cross_T+probe are ~4%. (3) The biggest standing structural idea remains the n1024/n2048 UNDERFILL (env: ~88 idle SMs at n1024) multi-CTA-per-matrix m-split with ~59% estimated headroom -- that targets idle hardware, a cleaner win than fighting Triton's already-good n512 panel.

GEOMEAN WEIGHTS ALL 12 SHAPES EQUALLY in ratio space, so cutting the tiny shapes pays exactly like cutting n512. The 3 tiny shapes are UNDER-ATTACKED and look REGRESSED: n32 B20 = 49.8us running at ~1% GPU (almost pure overhead/launch -- huge headroom; documented fast path was ~10us), n176 B40 = 193us, n352 B40 = 504us. Diagnose with nsys why _tiny_qr (n<=32, one-warp-per-matrix) and the n176/n352 _w2_qr small-batch path are this slow (kernel inefficiency vs dispatch overhead vs graph-capture gating _GRAPH_MINN=64 leaving n32 eager). Recover them: a faster tiny kernel (more matrices/warp parallelism, better occupancy for 20-40 matrices), and/or cheaper routing. A 2x cut on each tiny shape is ~0.94^3 = -17% geomean. Tiny shapes (n32/176/352): diagnosed at hard LATENCY/GRID-STARVATION floor, NO win. n32=48us GPU is the 32-step serial-Householder critical path (batch-independent B20-296=49us, ncu 3% occ 0.07 waves); both qr_tiny(49) and Triton _w2_qr(46) hit the floor. n176/n352 panel is 80%, grid-starved (ncu 0.14 waves, 6% occ, 201 r/thr, 40 CTAs/148 SMs). Shuffle-broadcast qr_tiny rewrite = 5x SLOWER (264us, ~2000 shfls beat by 1 syncwarp+cached smem). Structural alts dead: CholeskyQR orhr_col reconstruction = same serial path; TSQR dead(env); m-split = cross-CTA-reduction-per-reflector wall. Brief-3 tiny shapes (n32/176/352): NO improvement landed (parent 2168us). I diagnosed all three thoroughly and exhausted every tractable lever -- they sit at a hard SERIAL-HOUSEHOLDER LATENCY floor + GRID-STARVATION, NOT the dispatch overhead the brief expected. CORRECTION to the brief's premise: n32 is NOT '~1% GPU' -- torch-profiler shows its qr_tiny kernel = 48us = 94% of the 51us wall, and it is BATCH-INDEPENDENT (B=20/148/296 all ~49us, ncu 3% occ / 0.07 waves) -> the 49us IS the critical-path latency of the 32-step serial Householder sweep with nothing to hide it. The Triton _w2_qr path gives 46us; both hit the same ~46-49us floor. Graph capture is OFF for n32 and does NOT help (prior fleet: captured 52us > eager 48us, because the KERNEL is the cost). n176/n352 are panel-bound (80%): ncu shows the panel grid-STARVED (40 CTAs on 148 SMs = 94% idle, 0.14 waves, 6% occ, 201 r/thr near spill), so wall ~= critical path of the serial N/BLK-panel chain. LEVERS SWEPT, ALL CONFIRM CURRENT IS OPTIMAL: BLK (32 best; 64 spills n352 to 17ms; powers-of-2 only), panel num_warps (PNW=4 best; PNW=2 spills n352 to 12ms), qr_tiny WPB (2). The n512 two-level IB=16 panel is WORSE for n176/n352 (255 vs 209, 611 vs 525us -- its inner-trailing+cross_T overhead outweighs the un-spilled panel at B=40). I ALSO rewrote qr_tiny replacing its smem reflector buffer with warp-shuffle broadcast (the leading hypothesis for cutting per-step latency) -- it was bit-correct but 5x SLOWER (264 vs 49us): ~2000 per-element shfls are beaten by the existing one-syncwarp-per-step + cached smem reads, so the current smem design is near-optimal. STRUCTURAL ALTERNATIVES ARE DEAD ENDS: CholeskyQR would parallelize the Gram but the geqrf (H,tau) output needs the orhr_col Householder RECONSTRUCTION whose critical path is the SAME serial chain (the documented n4096 finding); TSQR/CAQR are confirmed dead (env notes); a panel m-split to use idle SMs needs a cross-CTA reduction PER reflector (32/panel) = the TSQR wall; and brief-2 proved hand-CUDA reductions are 5-7x slower than Triton tl.sum. The diagnosis is committed inline (comment-only, code byte-identical to NO_TRANS parent) so no future brief re-explores these. CONCLUSION: the tiny shapes are at the serial-Householder latency floor; the only win is an ALGORITHM with a genuinely shorter critical path that still emits geqrf reflectors, and none exists among the approaches available here. STRONG SUGGESTION: I have now returned 3 consecutive measured-negatives (fp8 trailing, fp16x1+classifier, cross-matrix-ILP panel, tiny shapes) and the COMMON ROOT is that the n512/tiny kernels are already near-optimal/latency-floored. The ONE clearly-winnable structural opportunity I keep surfacing and that NO worker has landed is the n1024/n2048 UNDERFILL: env notes ~88 IDLE SMs at n1024 (only 60 CTAs on 148 SMs) with a ~59%-headroom multi-CTA-per-matrix m-SPLIT of the TRAILING (not the panel -- the trailing is embarrassingly parallel and splits cleanly across the idle SMs with NO per-reflector cross-CTA sync, unlike the panel). That targets genuinely idle hardware on the 2nd-most-weighted shape group (n1024 = shapes 4,8,11), is invariance-safe (shape-N-gated), and is a far higher-EV use of a worker than fighting the already-optimal n512/tiny kernels. Point the next brief there.

Tiny/n512 are latency-floored (you proved it). Take your own highest-EV recommendation: the n=1024 B=60 / n=2048 B=8 TRAILING UNDERFILL. The PANEL m-split failed (per-reflector cross-CTA sync = TSQR wall), but the TRAILING is embarrassingly parallel and needs NO per-reflector sync -- split each matrix's trailing update (W=V^T C and C-=V@YT) across MULTIPLE CTAs along the m (row) dimension so the ~88 idle SMs at n1024 (60 CTAs->many) and ~140 idle at n2048 fill up. Each row-band CTA computes its partial W (needs a cross-CTA reduce of the BLKxncols W -- SMALL, once per outer block, NOT per reflector) then applies independently. This is the ~59%-headroom multi-CTA-trailing m-split, shape-N-gated (invariance-safe), distinct from W4's within-kernel finer tiling. Trailing m-split for n1024/n2048 underfill: BUILT (partial-W row-band kernel + YTsum cross-CTA reduce, once/block on small W -- dodges the panel TSQR wall), validated PASS, but measured break-even-to-WORSE (nrt 2-16, BNc_Y 64-256, gated/ungated, graph on/off: n2048 8730 base -> 9279 nrt2, BNc_Y128 9888us). ROOT: brief premise wrong -- the trailing's COL-TILE grid already saturates it (n1024 fused 1st block grid 1860 = 2.09 waves SATURATED, bottleneck is 17% occ/register-wall not grid; n2048 YT grid 256 = 0.86 waves only mildly underfilled, just 16.7%). The PANEL is the real underfill (grid=B 60/8) but that's the TSQR wall. Underfill and chain-length are ANTI-CORRELATED across the j-loop (early=long-chain+saturated, late=short-chain+underfilled) so row-band split has no sweet spot. Comment-only, code byte-identical to parent, benchmark 2171us.

Brief-4 trailing m-split: NO improvement landed (parent 2171us). I took my own recommendation and BUILT the full trailing m-split (a partial-W row-band kernel writing nrt partial W's + a YTsum kernel summing them and doing YT=T^T@W -- the cross-CTA reduce is correctly ONCE per outer block on the small BLKxncols W, dodging the panel-m-split's per-reflector TSQR wall). It validated PASS (correct), but measured break-even-to-WORSE across EVERY config I swept (nrt 2/4/8/16, BNc_Y 64/128/256, gated and ungated, graph on and off): n2048 8730us base -> 9279us (nrt2), and widening the col-tile to BNc_Y=128 to feed the row-bands -> 9888us. THE BRIEF'S PREMISE WAS WRONG (and I should have caught it before recommending it -- my bad): the TRAILING is NOT meaningfully underfilled. Its COL-TILE grid dimension (nct_y) already saturates the GPU -- ncu shows the n1024 fused-trailing first block runs grid=1860 = 2.09 waves (SATURATED; its real bottleneck is 17% occupancy / register-wall at 2 warps/CTA, NOT grid-fill), and the n2048 YT first block is grid=256 = 0.86 waves (only MILDLY underfilled) and is just 16.7% of n2048. The ~88 idle SMs the env notes describe are during the PANEL (grid=B = 60 for n1024, 8 for n2048), NOT the trailing -- and the panel is the TSQR wall (brief-2). DECISIVE STRUCTURAL FINDING: underfill and W-chain-length are ANTI-CORRELATED across the j-loop -- the EARLY blocks (long W-reduction chain, worth splitting) already saturate the grid via col-tiles, while the LATE blocks that ARE underfilled have small pheight (short chain, nothing to split). So a row-band m-split has NO sweet spot, and trading col-tile parallelism for row-band parallelism degrades the base tile efficiency + adds the Wpart HBM round-trip. Committed comment-only (code byte-identical to parent) with the finding inline. HONEST ASSESSMENT after 4 consecutive measured-negatives from me (fp8 trailing, fp16x1+classifier, cross-matrix-ILP panel, tiny shapes, trailing m-split): this kernel is MATURE and at/near its speed-of-light for the standard precision/tiling/ILP/occupancy levers -- every regime I have profiled is either latency-floored (n32, n512 panel, n1024 trailing occupancy-wall) or grid-starved with the only fill-path being the TSQR-walled panel. The remaining real bottleneck on the geomean-dominant shapes is uniformly the PANEL (55% n1024, 53% n2048, 33% n512, 80% n176/352), and it resists every non-TSQR structural attack. SUGGESTIONS for genuinely-unexplored angles (all bigger/riskier than what I tried): (1) a LEFT-LOOKING blocked QR instead of the current right-looking one -- different memory traffic (the trailing update is deferred and applied just-in-time), which MIGHT change the panel/trailing balance and the occupancy wall; (2) reducing the panel's 201-reg/thread footprint via a recursive within-panel blocking (smaller working tile) to lift occupancy where register-walled (n1024/n2048 panel); (3) accept the kernel is near-frontier and pivot the fleet to SUBMISSION/validation of the current best (the leaderboard gap to #1 1293us from our 2171us may be structural in a way none of these incremental levers close). I'd weight (3) highly -- I have strong evidence the incremental design space is largely exhausted.

Brief-5 vendor-QR probe: NO win, but HIGH-INFORMATION (this one is genuinely conclusive, not a frustrating dead-end). I built ctypes paths to BOTH vendor libs and benchmarked per-shape vs the custom kernel. THREE clean findings: (1) cusolverDnSgeqrfBatched DOES NOT EXIST -- cuSOLVER's dense batched API is svd/eig/Cholesky only (gesvdjBatched/heevjBatched/potrfBatched), there is NO batched QR in cuSOLVER. (2) But cublasSgeqrfBatched is a CORRECTNESS-ONLY REFERENCE kernel -- CATASTROPHICALLY slow: vs the custom path it is n32 6.9x / n176 101x / n352 256x / n512 156x / n1024 1233x (FOUR-POINT-NINE SECONDS) slower.
